Subject: Acme GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection - post-demo next steps

Hi Jane / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: Acme will be the controller for the product events and user data described in the call; Redwoods runs inference as a processor for model inference and managed hosting variants.
- Doc: I’ve attached our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and an SCC modules matrix (SCC_modules_matrix.xlsx) to show the typical mappings.

Can you confirm two things so we can route the right docs to Legal:
1) Confirm the intended controller/processor relationship (controller -> processor is what I have noted). If that’s correct, we’ll propose the Controller-to-Processor SCC module.
2) Would you prefer we (a) accept redlines in your DPA template or (b) propose ours and have your team redline? Either works — tell us which you prefer and expected turnaround.

Other asks: If you want us to complete your vendor security questionnaire, please either: (a) send the link back to me, or (b) use the secure questionnaire link I’ll share in a follow-up. We can also provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and encryption/KMS details under an NDA.

Suggested timeline: we can return an editable DPA + SCC proposal within 2 business days after you confirm controller/processor alignment and preference on redlines.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on sending any docx until you confirm the above.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
